events.title: Danish and Livonian conquest
hints: Crusading knights launched attacks on the pagan tribes from the south in 1208.
A decisive campaign in 1227 completed the conquest of the western islands.
events.summary: From 1208 the Livonian Brothers of the Sword and the Danes campaigned against the Estonian tribes, and the last pocket of resistance on the island of Saaremaa fell in 1227. The conquered territory was divided among the Danish crown and the German knights and bishops.

events.title: Danish Estonia
hints: A king landed at Lindanise in 1219 and established a fortress in the north.
In 1346 the territory was sold to the knights for a large sum in marks.
events.summary: Denmark took northern Estonia in 1219 and founded Reval, present-day Tallinn. After a revolt in 1343 it sold the province to the Teutonic Order in 1346 for 19,000 marks of silver.

events.title: Swedish Estonia
hints: A city's council submitted to a northern king in 1561 to escape a rival's armies.
Peasants supplied grain to an army fighting in Germany.
events.summary: Reval and northern Estonia passed under Swedish protection in 1561 amid the Livonian War, and Sweden later gained more of Livonia. The province supplied grain and soldiers for Sweden's wars until its conquest by Russia in 1710.

events.title: Russian imperial rule
hints: Tallinn capitulated in 1710 during the Great Northern War.
German-speaking nobles kept power, and the tsars pursued Russification in the 1880s.
events.summary: Russia conquered Estonia in 1710 and held it through the Treaty of Nystad in 1721 until 1918. Baltic German nobles kept their privileges, and from the 1880s an assertive Russification policy was imposed.

events.title: Soviet occupation and annexation of 1940
hints: Annexed after an ultimatum, bases treaty and rigged elections in the summer of 1940.
A secret protocol between two dictators had assigned it to a Soviet sphere of influence.
events.summary: Following the secret protocol of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, the Soviet Union forced military bases on the country in 1939, occupied it in June 1940, held staged elections and annexed it in August 1940.
events.wikipediaTitle: Soviet occupation of the Baltic states (1940)

events.title: Nazi German occupation
hints: Occupied after the 1941 invasion of the Soviet Union and run as part of an eastern administrative district.
Its oil shale industry was taken over for the war effort.
events.summary: German forces occupied the country in 1941 and incorporated it into the Reichskommissariat Ostland. The oil shale industry and local labour were exploited, and the occupation caused mass repression and the killing of most of the Jewish population.
events.wikipediaTitle: German occupation of Estonia during World War II

events.title: Soviet occupation 1944 to 1991
hints: Tens of thousands were deported in a single March operation in 1949.
A mass singing movement helped win back independence in 1991.
events.summary: The Red Army returned in 1944 and the country was incorporated into the Soviet Union for almost five decades. Collectivisation and mass deportations, notably Operation Priboi in March 1949, were followed by industrial development under Moscow's plans, and independence was restored in 1991.
